brief:
You are helping build a test of instruction-wording robustness. Rewrite the change request below as a different person would phrase it in a message to a BIM modeller. Requirements: (1) every fact stays exactly: numbers with units, quoted names in the same quotes, GlobalIds, Ifc class names, directions, storey names, and every relation; add nothing, drop nothing. (2) The wording must be substantially different: a different opening, different verbs (e.g. remove/delete/get rid of instead of take out; put in/create/model instead of add), a different order of the parts, and a natural human tone (a short reason, a 'please', a comment). (3) Returning the text unchanged or with only a word or two changed is a failure. Output only the rewritten request.

Request:
retry_note: A previous rewrite of this request was rejected: {why} Write a new rewrite that avoids this.
checks:
Rewrite the wording of the 100 val-v3b task instructions with a commercial model that wrote none of the
training wording (the v10 training paraphrases came from Qwen3.5-9B; this pass uses OpenAI gpt-5.6).

Procedure follows runs_local/stage_a_v6/val100_paraphrase/paraphrase.py: the same brief, the same
default temperature (none sent; GPT-5 models accept only the default), up to three attempts per task, and the original wording kept when no
attempt passes the checks. The checks are the earlier ones, made exact:
  * protected tokens must survive verbatim: every number (with its sign), every quoted name in the same
    single quotes (storey names are quoted names), every GlobalId (case-sensitive; quotes around a GlobalId
    optional), every Ifc class name, Pset name, upper-case enumeration value, axis token (+X, -Y),
    the W/m2K unit, and every direction / relation word of the original (direction, ordinal, negation,
    'only', 'true'/'false') and every element noun (door, window, wall, slab, column, space, storey, opening,
    with a few plain synonyms such as room, level, void);
  * every number-unit pair of the original survives, and the rewrite uses the same set of length units;
  * nothing is added: no number, GlobalId, quoted name, Ifc class, Pset, enumeration value or axis token
    that the original does not contain;
  * fewer than 80 % of the original's non-fact words are reused, and the first three words differ.
Differences from the earlier script, all on the checking side: the quoted-name pattern no longer runs
across possessives (wall's ... '), signed numbers keep their sign, GlobalIds are compared case-sensitively,
element nouns are protected, a retry carries one sentence naming the check the previous attempt failed,
and max_completion_tokens is 1600 (800 before) because reasoning tokens count against it.

After the run every machine-accepted pair was read by hand against its original. A rewrite that kept every
token but changed what the request asks for (a new reference point, a misleading object of the verb, a
changed order of edits, an added constraint) is listed in AUDIT_REJECT and its original wording is kept.
